GRAMMAR REFERENCE, 10-BET (125-bet). Yuqorida o'ngda 'Grammar Reference'.

CHAP USTUN (Unit 10 davomi):
'MIGHT/COULD': 'We use might or could to say that something is likely to happen. Stay away from the cat. It might/could scratch you.'
'HAVE TO/DON'T HAVE TO - MUST/MUSTN'T': • We use have to to express necessity. 'You have to buy a ticket before entering the theatre.' • We use do not have to to say that it is not necessary for something to happen. 'You don't have to help me with the washing-up. (... but you can if you want to.)' • We can also use must/mustn't to express very strong advice. 'You must stay away from those dogs. (It's very important that you stay away from those dogs.) You mustn't go near the water. (It's very important that you don't go near the water.)' • We also use mustn't to express prohibition. 'You mustn't drink and drive. (It's illegal.)'
'CAN - BE ALLOWED TO': • We use can to ask for or give permission. 'Can I go out? You can go now.' • We use can't to refuse permission. 'I'm afraid you can't go to the party.' • We use be allowed to to ask for, give or refuse permission. The permission, however, does not depend on the speaker. Compare the examples: 'Can I watch TV? (Will you allow me to watch TV?) Am I allowed to keep a pet in my room? (What is the rule?)'
To'q sariq 'UNIT 11'. 'TYPE 2 CONDITIONALS': • Type 2 conditionals express an imaginary or improbable situation which is unlikely to happen in the present or future. They are formed as follows:

O'NG USTUN:
QUTI: 'If + past simple ... would + bare infinitive'. 'If I had the time, I would learn how to paint. (I don't have the time now, so it is unlikely that I will learn how to paint. Improbable situation)' • We can use were instead of was for all persons. 'If Julie was/were here, she would help us with our homework.' • We also use if I were you ... to give advice. 'If I were you, I would stop smoking.'
Ko'k 'UNIT 12'. 'WHO/WHICH/WHERE': • We use the relative pronoun who instead of subject pronouns (I, you, he, etc) to refer to people. 'I met a woman who was a teacher.' • We use the relative pronoun which to refer to things. 'This is the pen which I found yesterday.' • We use the relative adverb where to refer to places. 'I went to Lisbon where I met some friends.'
'SOME/ANY/NO + COMPOUNDS'. KO'K JADVAL 'Affirmative': Determiners: some | Pronouns - people: someone/somebody, things: something | Adverbs - places: somewhere. JADVAL 'Interrogative': Determiners: any | Pronouns - people: anyone/anybody, things: anything | Adverbs - places: anywhere.

Bet raqami: pastda o'ngda '125'.

sections.title: Unit 10 - Modals: might/could, have to, must, can, be allowed to
sections.titleUz: 10-unit - Modal fe'llar: might/could, have to, must, can, be allowed to

exercises.instructionEn: Might/Could. Have to / Don't have to - Must / Mustn't. Can - Be allowed to.
exercises.instructionUz: Might/Could. Have to / Don't have to - Must / Mustn't. Can - Be allowed to.
exercises.explanationUz:
MODAL FE'LLAR (10-unit).


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  MIGHT / COULD - EHTIMOL         ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  = bo'lishi mumkin:
  'Stay away from the cat. It
   MIGHT/COULD scratch you.'


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  HAVE TO - ZARURAT               ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  HAVE TO = kerak (zarurat):
    'You HAVE TO buy a ticket.'
  DON'T HAVE TO = shart emas
    (xohlasang qilasan):
    "You DON'T HAVE TO help me."


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  MUST / MUSTN'T                  ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  MUST = kuchli maslahat/majburiyat:
    'You MUST stay away from those
     dogs.'
  MUSTN'T = qat'iy maslahat /
  TAQIQ:
    "You MUSTN'T go near the water."
    "You MUSTN'T drink and drive."
    (noqonuniy)

  ⚠ 'don't have to' ≠ 'mustn't'!
  don't have to = shart emas
  mustn't = taqiqlangan


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  CAN - RUXSAT                    ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  CAN = ruxsat so'rash/berish:
    'CAN I go out?' 'You CAN go
     now.'
  CAN'T = ruxsat bermaslik:
    "I'm afraid you CAN'T go to the
     party."


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  BE ALLOWED TO - QOIDA           ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  Ruxsat GAPIRUVChIGA BOG'LIQ EMAS
  (qoida):
  'Can I watch TV?' = Sen ruxsat
    berasanmi?
  'AM I ALLOWED TO keep a pet?' =
    Qoida qanday?


⚠ 'TO SCRATCH':

  = tirnamoq.


⚠ 'NECESSITY':

  = zarurat.


⚠ 'PROHIBITION':

  = taqiq.


⚠ 'PERMISSION':

  = ruxsat.


⚠ 'TO REFUSE':

  = rad etmoq.

points.en: We use might or could to say that something is likely to happen. Stay away from the cat. It might/could scratch you.
points.uz: 'Might' yoki 'could' ni biror narsa bo'lishi mumkinligini aytish uchun ishlatamiz. Mushukdan uzoq tur. U seni tirnashi mumkin.

points.en: We use have to to express necessity. You have to buy a ticket before entering the theatre. We use do not have to to say that it is not necessary for something to happen. You don't have to help me with the washing-up. (... but you can if you want to.)
points.uz: 'Have to' ni zaruratni bildirish uchun ishlatamiz. Teatrga kirishdan oldin chipta sotib olishing kerak. 'Do not have to' ni biror narsa shart emasligini aytish uchun ishlatamiz. Idish yuvishda menga yordam berishing shart emas. (... lekin xohlasang, mumkin.)
points.noteUz: ⚠ have to = kerak; don't have to = shart emas.

points.en: We can also use must/mustn't to express very strong advice. You must stay away from those dogs. You mustn't go near the water. We also use mustn't to express prohibition. You mustn't drink and drive. (It's illegal.)
points.uz: 'Must/mustn't' ni juda kuchli maslahat uchun ham ishlatishimiz mumkin. O'sha itlardan uzoq turishing kerak. Suv yoniga bormasliging kerak. 'Mustn't' ni taqiqni bildirish uchun ham ishlatamiz. Ichib mashina haydash mumkin emas. (Bu noqonuniy.)

points.en: We use can to ask for or give permission. Can I go out? You can go now. We use can't to refuse permission. I'm afraid you can't go to the party.
points.uz: 'Can' ni ruxsat so'rash yoki berish uchun ishlatamiz. Chiqsam bo'ladimi? Hozir ketishing mumkin. 'Can't' ni ruxsat bermaslik uchun ishlatamiz. Afsuski, bazmga borishing mumkin emas.

points.en: We use be allowed to to ask for, give or refuse permission. The permission, however, does not depend on the speaker. Can I watch TV? (Will you allow me to watch TV?) Am I allowed to keep a pet in my room? (What is the rule?)
points.uz: 'Be allowed to' ni ruxsat so'rash, berish yoki rad etish uchun ishlatamiz. Lekin ruxsat gapiruvchiga bog'liq emas. Televizor ko'rsam bo'ladimi? (Ruxsat berasanmi?) Xonamda uy hayvoni saqlashga ruxsat bormi? (Qoida qanday?)
points.noteUz: ⚠ be allowed to = qoida bo'yicha ruxsat.

exercises.instructionEn: Type 2 conditionals express an imaginary or improbable situation which is unlikely to happen in the present or future. If + past simple ... would + bare infinitive. If I had the time, I would learn how to paint. We can use were instead of was for all persons. If Julie was/were here, she would help us. We also use if I were you ... to give advice. If I were you, I would stop smoking.
exercises.instructionUz: 2-tur shart gaplari hozir yoki kelajakda bo'lishi ehtimoldan yiroq xayoliy vaziyatni bildiradi. If + o'tgan oddiy ... would + 'to'siz infinitiv. Agar vaqtim bo'lsa, rasm chizishni o'rganardim. Barcha shaxslarda was o'rniga were ishlatishimiz mumkin. Agar Julie shu yerda bo'lsa, bizga yordam berardi. Maslahat berish uchun 'if I were you ...' ni ham ishlatamiz. Sening o'rningda bo'lsam, chekishni tashlardim.
exercises.explanationUz:
2-TUR ShART GAPI - XAYoLIY.

  IF + PAST SIMPLE, WOULD + FE'L

  'If I HAD the time, I WOULD LEARN
   how to paint.'
  (vaqtim YO'Q - xayol)


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  1-TUR va 2-TUR FARQI            ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  1-TUR: real, ehtimolli
    'If I HAVE time, I WILL learn.'
  2-TUR: xayoliy, ehtimoldan yiroq
    'If I HAD time, I WOULD learn.'

  ⚠ 2-turda past simple bo'lsa ham
  HOZIR/KELAJAK haqida!


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  WERE - HAMMA ShAXSDA            ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  'If Julie WAS/WERE here, she
   would help us.'
  ⚠ 'were' rasmiyroq va to'g'riroq.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  IF I WERE YOU - MASLAHAT        ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  'IF I WERE YOU, I would stop
   smoking.'
  = Sening o'rningda bo'lsam ...


⚠ 'IMAGINARY':

  = xayoliy.


⚠ 'IMPROBABLE':

  = ehtimoldan yiroq.


⚠ 'UNLIKELY':

  = ehtimoldan yiroq.

points.en: Type 2 conditionals express an imaginary or improbable situation which is unlikely to happen in the present or future. If + past simple ... would + bare infinitive. If I had the time, I would learn how to paint. (I don't have the time now, so it is unlikely that I will learn how to paint.)
points.uz: 2-tur shart gaplari hozir yoki kelajakda bo'lishi ehtimoldan yiroq xayoliy vaziyatni bildiradi. If + o'tgan oddiy ... would + 'to'siz infinitiv. Agar vaqtim bo'lsa, rasm chizishni o'rganardim. (Hozir vaqtim yo'q, shuning uchun o'rganishim ehtimoldan yiroq.)

points.en: We can use were instead of was for all persons. If Julie was/were here, she would help us with our homework.
points.uz: Barcha shaxslarda was o'rniga were ishlatishimiz mumkin. Agar Julie shu yerda bo'lsa, uy vazifamizda yordam berardi.

points.en: We also use if I were you ... to give advice. If I were you, I would stop smoking.
points.uz: Maslahat berish uchun 'if I were you ...' ni ham ishlatamiz. Sening o'rningda bo'lsam, chekishni tashlardim.

exercises.instructionEn: Who/Which/Where. We use the relative pronoun who to refer to people. I met a woman who was a teacher. We use the relative pronoun which to refer to things. This is the pen which I found yesterday. We use the relative adverb where to refer to places. I went to Lisbon where I met some friends. Some/Any/No + compounds: some - someone/somebody, something, somewhere (affirmative); any - anyone/anybody, anything, anywhere (interrogative).
exercises.instructionUz: Who/Which/Where. Nisbiy olmosh 'who' ni odamlar uchun ishlatamiz. Men o'qituvchi bo'lgan ayolni uchratdim. Nisbiy olmosh 'which' ni narsalar uchun ishlatamiz. Bu men kecha topgan ruchka. Nisbiy ravish 'where' ni joylar uchun ishlatamiz. Men do'stlarimni uchratgan Lissabonga bordim. Some/Any/No birikmalari: some - someone/somebody, something, somewhere (tasdiq); any - anyone/anybody, anything, anywhere (so'roq).
exercises.explanationUz:
NISBIY OLMOShLAR (12-unit):

  WHO - ODAMLAR (I, you, he o'rnida):
    'I met a woman WHO was a
     teacher.'
  WHICH - NARSALAR:
    'This is the pen WHICH I found
     yesterday.'
  WHERE - JOYLAR (nisbiy ravish):
    'I went to Lisbon WHERE I met
     some friends.'

  ⚠ 'that' - who va which o'rnida
  ham bo'ladi.


SOME/ANY/NO BIRIKMALARI:

  TASDIQ (some):
    some (aniqlovchi)
    someone/somebody (odam)
    something (narsa)
    somewhere (joy)

  SO'ROQ (any):
    any (aniqlovchi)
    anyone/anybody (odam)
    anything (narsa)
    anywhere (joy)

  ⚠ Inkor (no) - keyingi betda.


⚠ 'A RELATIVE PRONOUN':

  = nisbiy olmosh.


⚠ 'A DETERMINER':

  = aniqlovchi (otdan oldin).


⚠ 'A COMPOUND':

  = birikma, qo'shma so'z.

points.en: We use the relative pronoun who instead of subject pronouns (I, you, he, etc) to refer to people. I met a woman who was a teacher.
points.uz: Nisbiy olmosh 'who' ni ega olmoshlari (I, you, he va h.k.) o'rnida odamlar uchun ishlatamiz. Men o'qituvchi bo'lgan ayolni uchratdim.

points.en: We use the relative pronoun which to refer to things. This is the pen which I found yesterday.
points.uz: Nisbiy olmosh 'which' ni narsalar uchun ishlatamiz. Bu men kecha topgan ruchka.

points.en: We use the relative adverb where to refer to places. I went to Lisbon where I met some friends.
points.uz: Nisbiy ravish 'where' ni joylar uchun ishlatamiz. Men do'stlarimni uchratgan Lissabonga bordim.

points.en: Some/Any/No + compounds. Affirmative: some - someone/somebody (people), something (things), somewhere (places). Interrogative: any - anyone/anybody, anything, anywhere.
points.uz: Some/Any/No birikmalari. Tasdiq: some - someone/somebody (odamlar), something (narsalar), somewhere (joylar). So'roq: any - anyone/anybody, anything, anywhere.

patterns.formula: You have to / don't have to + FE'L.
patterns.exampleEn: You have to buy a ticket. You don't have to help me.
patterns.exampleUz: Chipta sotib olishing kerak. Menga yordam berishing shart emas.

patterns.exampleEn: Am I allowed to keep a pet in my room?
patterns.exampleUz: Xonamda uy hayvoni saqlashga ruxsat bormi?

patterns.formula: If I were you, I would + FE'L.
patterns.exampleEn: If I were you, I would stop smoking.
